description: We are Astrology, a highly motivated team of developers and researchers focused on Cybersecurity (CTF), MilTech, and Robotic Systems. Our expertise spans low-level programming, network security, data analysis, and hardware integration. We thrive on solving complex, fast-paced technical challenges and turning ambitious ideas into functional prototypes.
summary: AGROSAS OS is a farm operating system that turns open NASA Earth data into concrete decisions for one real field. Point at a field and the platform builds its passport from satellite, climate, terrain and soil data, simulates thousands of crop rotations day by day against the field’s own 30-year climate and seven climate scenarios up to 2050, and explains which rotation protects the soil, saves water and keeps income stable — and why. Every insight ends in an action: a 72-hour plan with frost warnings, spraying windows and inspections, 3D management zones on real terrain, Sentinel-2 change maps that show exactly where the field changed, and an agronomist assistant that answers with the field’s real numbers. It matters because the climate under every field is shifting, and the data to see it is free but built for scientists, not farmers. AGROSAS OS is the bridge from space to soil.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
AGROSAS OS answers the questions a farmer actually asks — what do I sow next season, will my rotation survive a dry year, where is my field losing, can I spray on Tuesday? — using open NASA and partner data for one real field.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Sense: for any field polygon the platform pulls 30 years of daily ERA5 climate, NASA POWER agro-climate series, SRTM terrain, SoilGrids soil texture and carbon, Sentinel-2 10 m imagery and NASA GIBS daily MODIS/VIIRS layers.
2. Passport: it derives the field's risks automatically — drought and water balance, erosion on slopes, frost and winter-kill, heat during flowering, waterlogging and low soil carbon.
3. Model: a rotation engine simulates thousands of 4–5-year rotations day by day (water balance, nitrogen, erosion, margin) and stress-tests them under seven scenarios: current climate, trend to 2035, dry year, wet year, hot summer, drought + heat and a +2.5 °C 2050 climate. The farmer picks a goal — stable income, maximum profit, drought survival or soil restoration — and every recommendation shows margin, water deficit, erosion and why it was chosen.
4. Act: forecasts, zones and imagery become a 72-hour action plan (frost warnings, spraying windows, inspections) with one-click task completion; 3D management zones on a 20 m grid show where water collects and slopes erode, with a soil-sampling route; Sentinel-2 before/after comparison picks cloud-free dates automatically and maps exactly where vegetation, leaf water and chlorophyll changed.

ALSO INSIDE
A live 3D globe with real satellites propagated by SGP4 (Terra, Landsat, SMAP, ISS, Starlink), the Solar System with today's planet positions, a climate time machine with warming stripes for the exact field, NASA mission pages with official 3D models, a NASA news feed explained for farmers, a digital farm with an energy and water model, and Ukraine-specific resilience tools. The whole interface works in English and Ukrainian.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
Farmers get a field-level, explainable plan instead of raw grids; agronomists get evidence they can check, because every number shows its source, date and resolution. It works for any field on Earth, with special attention to Ukrainian farms facing climate and war-time pressure. When a source is unavailable the platform says so and never invents a measurement.

TOOLS
Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, three.js, MapLibre GL, Recharts, satellite.js; Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic; PostgreSQL 17 + PostGIS; Docker Compose, Caddy; 112 automated tests (pytest, Vitest, Playwright).
